inspiration: Loot as a weighted tier table: each item carries six per-tier weights, the sum per tier is cached once so a roll is a single draw; equipment and weapons pull enchantments from different tables (src/Engine/Tables/ItemTable.cpp:204-233). Recreate: our rarity table as zone data with a cached sum.

Faction hostility as a grid between monster groups, filled from a flat table and defaulting to friendly (src/Engine/Tables/HostilityTable.cpp:14-22). This is the data source for many-vs-one target choice and the hate list, and it fits MAX_ATTACKERS = 3.

Each map row sets its own reverb preset and its own music track (src/Engine/Tables/MapTable.cpp:21 and :90). Recreate as zone ambience beds: one reverb and one bed per zone, switched on border crossing.

Monster descriptor card: body height, collision radius, to-hit radius, movement speed, a tint colour, a sound id per action slot, and one sprite name per animation state (src/Engine/Objects/Monsters.h:94-101). This is the shape for row 7 (creature actor and clips): one card per creature, animation states as keys.

Pivot offsets per prop type (src/Engine/Tables/ChestTable.cpp:5-8): a small table of x/y anchor, width and height per chest type, so eight prop types sit on the same spot whatever the sprite. Use it for any prop set that must read at 375 wide.

Text-file tables with a column comment above each loader (items.txt, monsters.txt, mapstats.txt, hostile.txt, placemon.txt, rnditems.txt; src/Engine/Objects/Monsters.cpp:244 and :255, src/Engine/Tables/MapTable.cpp:19). Pattern for our catalogue as runtime source (row 20 and 21): one table per concept, column order in the comment.

Shader file names suggest a decal pass (gldecalshader), a separate fog and lighting include (fog.glsl, lighting.glsl) and a billboard pass (glbillbshader). Names only, not read: a decal pass for blood and wounds (row 8) is a shader idea to look at, not to copy.

briefs.label: Tiered loot chest set
briefs.why: Eight prop types share one footprint and each has its own anchor, so a chest reads the same as the one next to it; the silhouette carries the tier.
briefs.keep: one anchor and footprint per prop type; a tier read from silhouette before colour; same placement rule for every chest
briefs.change: our own banded iron and hasp designs, not the donor's chest look; a rarity colour ring we add; our own footprint sizes tuned to 375 wide
briefs.ref: src/Engine/Tables/ChestTable.cpp:5-8 (per-type offset, width and height arrays; the art itself is in the original game data and was not read)

briefs.label: Monster temperament tiers
briefs.why: A handful of temperaments (suicidal, timid, normal, aggressive) and movement ranges (stationary, short, medium, long, global, free) give readable behaviour from data alone.
briefs.keep: four temperaments as data; movement range as a named class; the tier is set per creature in the table, not in code
briefs.change: our own temperament names and ranges tied to leash and aggro row 4; add a threat-scaled-by-protection term; our own numbers
briefs.ref: src/Engine/Objects/Monsters.cpp:255 (table comment lists the ai and movement fields; the maps for each value sit just below it, lines not exact, not fully read)

briefs.label: Cave zone ambience bed
briefs.why: One reverb preset and one music track per map gives a zone its mood before any art is seen, and it costs no assets.
briefs.keep: reverb and music set as one row per zone; switch on zone border; cave-type preset used for underground
briefs.change: our own reverb preset values and a bespoke drone bed; add a per-zone filter on the bed, not on the reverb
briefs.ref: src/Engine/Tables/MapTable.cpp:21 and :90 (preset map and music id per map row)

briefs.label: Weighted treasure roll with enchant split
briefs.why: One cached weight sum per tier makes a loot roll a single draw; splitting enchantments between equipment and weapons keeps the two lists separate and easy to tune.
briefs.keep: six tier weights per item; cached sum; separate enchant tables for gear and weapons
briefs.change: our own rarity colours and drop sound per tier; a drop ceremony at 375 wide; our own weights and tier names
briefs.ref: src/Engine/Tables/ItemTable.cpp:204-233 (random item chance and enchantment chance loaders)
